Convert a coverage object to a data frame

Source: R/data_frame.R
as.data.frame.coverage.Rd

Convert a coverage object to a data frame

Usage

# S3 method for class 'coverage'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, sort = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

a coverage object.

row.names, optional

ignored, for compatibility with base::as.data.frame().

sort

if TRUE (the default), sum the counts of identical expressions and sort the rows by file and position. If FALSE, there is one row for each element of x, in the same order.

...

ignored.

Value

A data frame with one row for each traced expression of R code and each line of compiled code, and the columns:

  • filename: the source file, relative to the root attribute of x (the package directory, for package_coverage()) if there is one.

  • functions: the name of the function containing the expression, or NA for compiled code.

  • first_line, last_line: the lines the expression starts and ends on.

  • first_byte, last_byte: the bytes of those lines the expression starts and ends at.

  • first_column, last_column: the columns the expression starts and ends at. These differ from the bytes when the line contains multibyte characters.

  • first_parsed, last_parsed: the lines as seen by the parser. These differ from first_line and last_line when the source uses #line directives.

  • value: the number of times the expression was executed.

Use tally_coverage() for one row for each line instead.

Examples

cov <- code_coverage("add <- function(x, y) { x + y }", "add(1, 2)")
as.data.frame(cov)
#>                              filename functions first_line first_byte last_line
#> 1 /tmp/Rtmp3zUiIp/source.R18f5c5cbc40       add          1         25         1
#>   last_byte first_column last_column first_parsed last_parsed value
#> 1        29           25          29            1           1     1
